counterfactual_missing_items: Laboratory studies (CBC, basic metabolic panel, HIV, T-spot, syphilis screen, and ANCA panel) were normal
decisive_items: presumed serous retinal detachment secondary to posterior scleritis
an overlying retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid
response.rationale: C1 best integrates the causative posterior scleritis with the observed serous retinal detachment, matching the vignette's explicit conclusion. R3 captures scleral inflammation but omits the retinal detachment phenotype; R1 captures the serous detachment but misses the underlying scleral cause; R2 is nonspecific and supported only by mild inflammatory cells. The absence of retinal breaks and intraocular mass supports a non-rhegmatogenous inflammatory serous detachment.

rejected.why: Describes the serous retinal detachment as a manifestation but omits the underlying posterior scleritis and scleral enhancement.
Uveitis is too broad and nonspecific; the mild anterior and vitreous cells do not explain the scleral enhancement, choroidal detachments, or shifting subretinal fluid.
